SearchHow we decideRulings

Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

perform verb

carry out (a task, a duty)

also carry out, fulfil, do one’s duty, perform a task

classical

Phaedr. App. 19.2–3: obstetrīcis partibus sē posse fungī dīxit
Traupman 359

fungor, fungī, fūnctus sum

verb, third conjugation, deponent; with the ablative

perform, carry out (a duty, a task, an office)

With the ablative: officiō fungī, to do one’s duty; mūnere fungī, to hold a post and do its work (see position, a job).

Other words

  • praestō, praestāre, praestitī, praestitum — perform, fulfil (a duty)

    verb, first conjugation, transitive · also used · classical · Phaedr. 3.7.8: praestāre dominō sī pār officium potes; Cic. de Or. 2.38 (Lewis & Short): suum mūnus; Traupman 359

  • exsequor, exsequī, exsecūtus sum — carry out (orders, a plan)

    verb, third conjugation, deponent, transitive · also used · classical · Cic. Phil. 9.9 (Lewis & Short): mandāta vestra; Cic. Sen. 34 (Lewis & Short): omnia rēgis officia et mūnera

Examples

  • premente partū scrōfa cum gemeret jacēns, accurrit lupus et obstetrīcis partibus sē posse fungī dīxit, prōmittēns opem

    As a sow lay groaning in labour, a wolf ran up and said he could do a midwife’s part, promising help.Phaedr. App. 19.1–3

  • Suō quisque mūnere fungātur.

    Let everyone do his own job.composed

See also perform, chore, job, position.

SourcesLewis & Short: fungor · Lewis & Short: praesto · Lewis & Short: exsequor
